title: Taiwan's First Two F-16V Block 70 Jets Abort Delivery Flight, Turn Back to Hawaii
detail: The first two of Taiwan's 66 on-order F-16 C/D Block 70 ("Viper") fighters — single-seat jets with serial numbers 6727 and 6728 — took off from Hickam Field, Hawaii on September 7, 2026 on the next leg of their delivery route (Hawaii to Guam, then Guam to Chihhang Air Base in Taitung County) but turned back to Hawaii shortly after takeoff. Neither Lockheed Martin nor Taiwan's air force publicly explained the reason; unconfirmed reports pointed to a technical problem with one aircraft, while officials ruled out neither a mechanical fault nor weather. The jets — originally due for delivery in 2023 and delayed by production-line relocation and supply-chain disruptions — had already spent roughly two weeks stuck in Hawaii after departing Lockheed's Greenville, South Carolina plant on August 17. The aircraft are slated to join the air force's 7th Tactical Fighter Wing at Chihhang, defending Taiwan's eastern approaches; the remaining 64 jets are scheduled for delivery through 2027-2028.

title: Legislator May Chin's Longtime Aide Cuts Ankle Monitor, Disappears While Facing Corruption Trial
detail: Chang Chun-chieh, the former chief-of-staff to independent Legislator May Chin who has managed her China-affairs portfolio since 2002, disappeared on Sunday, September 6-7, 2026 after cutting off his court-ordered electronic ankle monitor, which judicial police later recovered "broken and thrown away." An arrest warrant was issued and immigration authorities notified. Chang and Chin were among 25 people indicted in June 2026 on corruption and fraud charges tied to the alleged embezzlement of public funds and the illegal import, during the 2022 pandemic, of 74,400 unapproved COVID-19 rapid test kits from China; prosecutors have recommended a 16-year sentence for Chang and 12.5 years for Chin. Chang had been released on NT$10 million bail in June on health grounds (he is over 70 and battling lung cancer) and had appeared in court the previous Tuesday, denying the corruption charges while admitting to document forgery. His disappearance preceded prosecutors' subsequent disclosure that they suspect he ran a China-funded espionage network from Chin's office.
